Subject: Sudden latency/error spike after model upgrade (v5.1 qprofile)

Karthik —

We pushed Redwood's v5.1 with the new qprofile yesterday night across our production inference fleet. Within the first two hours we started seeing p95 jump from ~180ms to 720ms and p99 to ~1.6s. Also noticing a small but steady increase in 5xx rate (auth errors and 504s). This is impacting the triage UI and a few clinicians are reporting timeouts.

Attached: a CSV with token-level p95/p99 trends and a sample trace (sample_request_trace.txt).

Can you please check if this matches any known behavior of the qprofile change or if this looks like a serving-side routing/packing problem? We need an initial read in the hour and a mitigation plan ASAP.

Thanks,
Avery Cole

Subject: Re: Sudden latency/error spike after model upgrade (v5.1 qprofile)

Avery — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments, they help. We see the same signal on our side for your tenant. Initial notes:
- Deployed v5.1 with a new quant profile that reduces memory per-token but changes kernel selection for attention on the 80-512 token path.
- Early hypothesis: the qprofile is increasing per-request kernel-switch overhead for your typical sequence mix, causing higher p95/p99. The 5xxs look correlated to overloaded worker threads hitting timeouts.

Immediate next steps (we can start now):
1) Roll your traffic to our v5.1-compatible fallback (v5.0-compatible runtime path) for 10% of traffic to measure differential — takes ~5m to route.
2) Collect a 15-minute hotpath trace with KV cache headers (we'll request those traces from the backend).
3) If rollback reduces p95 by >30%, escalate a temporary rollback for 100% while we optimize qprofile.

I'm pulling Laura in for exec-level coordination and Rishi for runtime tuning. Will update in 20m with the first measurements.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Sudden latency/error spike after model upgrade (v5.1 qprofile)

Action log from runtime team after digging into traces:
- Confirmed pattern: kernel selection oscillation for sequences between 64–256 tokens caused by the new quant kernels. This creates extra micro-batches and more frequent GPU kernel launches per request for your traffic mix.
- 5xx origins: worker thread queue saturation at the model container boundary under the new batching cadence. Not a networking/auth issue.

Quick mitigations applied (16:05 PDT):
- Enabled a per-tenant route to the v5.0-compatible kernel path (10% traffic). Initial A/B (15m): p95 for control: 210ms, for v5.1: 730ms — delta ~+3.5x. p99 shows similar. 5xx rate reduced in control by 78% vs v5.1.
- Throttled max concurrency for v5.1 workers for LatticeHealth to reduce queue saturation (temporary).

Next recommended steps:
1) Prepare rollback to v5.0-compat path for 100% if exec approves (rollback is ~3m).
2) Engineering task: adjust qprofile kernel hints for the 64–256 path and push a hotfix build; ETA 48 hours to test/validate.
3) Run a quick throughput baseline after rollback to validate no regression in token cost.

I'll attach a short stack trace and the sample hotpath results to the ticket.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
